heading: INT. GRAND CENTRAL WAITING HALL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. GRAND CENTRAL WAITING HALL - NIGHT
High arched windows, benches of dark oak.
A great board of arrivals flicks over names.
Steam from distant trains.
A few soldiers asleep on their duffels.
IMELDA CASTELLANOS, 40s, in a worn wool coat, sits on a bench with her hands in her lap.
A suitcase at her feet.
A man's hat on top of it.
WINIFRED BOYLE, 60s, in tweed, with a prim hat and a leather handbag, perches at the far end of the bench.
She has been watching the board for hours.
ARTHUR PEMBROKE, 30s, in a demobbed uniform with the insignia ripped from the sleeve, walks the aisle.
Stops.
Stares at Imelda.
Imelda?
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: She stands.
The hat falls from the suitcase.
Arthur bends to pick it up, but Winifred gets there first.
She holds it out to Imelda with a trembling hand, and Imelda takes it without taking her eyes off him.
Arthur. You are late.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: The trains. I was told.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: You were told four years ago.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: I am here now.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: Winifred rises, smooths her coat, and walks away down the hall.
She does not look back.
Arthur steps closer.
Imelda lifts the hat between them.
Your father's.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: I thought it was lost.
units.name: ARTHUR

units.text: Nothing is lost, Arthur. Only misplaced.
units.name: IMELDA

units.text: He puts it on his head.
It fits.
She straightens it with two fingers.
